original_value: This paper proposes a novel nonsingular terminal sliding mode control combined with global sliding surface for a class of uncertain nonlinear second-order systems. The suggested control approach is developed based on the Lyapunov theory. The sliding mode reaching the sliding surface in finite time can be guaranteed. Furthermore, chattering phenomenon caused by the switching control action can be eliminated theoretically, and desirable control performance is realized. The simulation and tank test results for heave control of a remotely operated vehicle are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents a new nonsingular terminal sliding mode control scheme combined with a global sliding surface for a class of uncertain nonlinear second-order systems. The proposed controller is designed using Lyapunov theory, and finite-time convergence to the sliding surface can be ensured. In addition, the chattering caused by switching control can be theoretically removed, yielding desirable control performance. Simulation and tank test results for heave control of a remotely operated vehicle are also provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.
